newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: DOLLAR WELL BID IN SINGAPORE, UK RATE NEWS AWAITED.
newsitem.headline: DOLLAR WELL BID IN SINGAPORE, UK RATE NEWS AWAITED.

text.p: The dollar shrugged off its early lethargy to head higher against the mark and yen on buying by U.S. names after midday on Thursday, Singapore dealers said.
But they said players are increasingly nervous about verbal or actual intervention by the Bundesbank as the 1.90 mark target comes into view.
The dollar hit a fresh 94-month high of 1.8913 marks on Wednesday.
"I think 1.90 will be a very strong resistance. Everybody is a bit wary of the Bundesbank," a European bank dealer said.
He said the mark/yen cross had been lifted by short-covering after early efforts to trigger stop-loss sales below the 62.70 level failed.
Tokyo dealers said the dollar was well bid against the yen on renewed worries about the health of mid-sized Japanese construction firms.
Meanwhile Singapore dealers said cable was likely to run into selling pressure on any moves above 1.61, unless there was renewed buying of sterling/mark.
Sterling/mark was dragged down by a slump in cable on Wednesday as the market questioned the likelihood of a U.K. rate hike on Thursday.

Traders said the Bank of England (BOE) could conceivably refrain from raising rates to stem the pound's rise and protect exports. The BOE's regular two-day meeting on interest rates ends on Thursday and an announcement is due at 1100 GMT.
